# The map

Which MRI physics this scanner covers, and which task asks for which piece of it.

The list holds 115 pieces of MRI physics and applied MR physics, as textbooks and curricula name them. The scanner forms 64 of them and 15 more in part. The other 36 are not formed yet: 15 of them the package already computes and checks without serving them, and [the last list](#not-formed-yet) says which piece of engine work each one waits for. Statistics of its images and signals have been compared with public phantom measurements on real scanners ([measured](physics/measured.md)); no image of its sequences has been compared pixel by pixel with a scan of the same object.

## On one screen

Rows: what you need to know. Columns: what you do with it. A cell holds the tasks; *italic* means in construction, not playable yet.

Listed: items on the map. Formed: an agent meets it at the console, and a check that exists shows it. Isolated by a task: one task is about this item. Used by a task: a task takes it, as its own item or beside it. Tasks in construction are not counted, and neither is what the package computes without serving it.

## The two axes

| | Subject | A piece of physics is filed here when |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Signal and contrast: what signal a tissue gives | it can be asked about one voxel |
| **B** | Spatial encoding and reconstruction: where the signal lands in the image | it can be asked on an object of uniform contrast |
| **C** | The system: what the machine adds: field, RF, gradients, noise, limits | it would be trivial on an ideal scanner |
| **D** | Image quality and artefacts: how good the image is, and what went wrong | it is about the whole image: SNR, contrast, resolution, time, artefacts |

| | Kind of task | What is delivered | For example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Measure | a quantity with its unit | T1 of a vial; the error of the centre frequency |
| **2** | Set | the setting that meets one requirement | the inversion time that nulls a tissue; the field of view without wrap |
| **3** | Trade | one protocol that meets several requirements at once | contrast, SNR and pixel size inside a time limit |
| **4** | Request | a scan for a stated purpose: the method is not named and the system has hidden properties | the fastest T1 map of a stated precision on an unfamiliar scanner |
| **5** | Design | the sequence itself: an RF pulse, a gradient waveform, the order and timing of its parts | a shorter slice-selective pulse inside the limits on peak B1 and RF power |

Kinds 1 to 3 are the knowledge, one piece at a time and then several together. Kind 4 asks for the best scan the console can give. Kind 5 lets the agent build what the console does not offer. A task of kind 3 or more names the simple items it brings together; whether training on the simple ones carries upward is a measurement, not a claim of this page.

## Formed in part

| | Item | What is missing | Waits for |
|---|---|---|---|
| A14 | Echo trains: fast (turbo) spin echo, echo train length, effective echo time | A console whose card lists them serves a fast spin echo and a multi-echo spin echo from the signal core: echo-train length, echo spacing, effective echo time, T2 blurring, the stimulated echoes of the slice profile and of the transmit field, the RF power of the train. One refocusing angle per train, an ideal crusher at the end of the repetition, at most 32 echoes, fat without J coupling. No shipped environment has such a console, and the tool layer of the environments does not offer the sequences yet | core in the console |
| A21 | Diffusion weighting: b-value, apparent diffusion coefficient, tensor | A console whose card lists it serves a diffusion-weighted spin echo from the signal core: the b-value of the lobes it plays, the echo time they cost, signal x exp(-b D) for the one free, isotropic coefficient of a tissue. No tensor (the design layer computes the b-tensor of a gradient program), no kurtosis, no perfusion fraction, no stimulated-echo or echo-planar readout; 16 of the 25 coefficients of the tissue table are declared. No shipped environment has such a console | core in the console |
| A25 | Susceptibility-weighted imaging: the phase of a gradient echo as contrast | Phase images show the field of air cavities; no tissue of the scanner has a susceptibility of its own (no veins, no iron). The 3D head declares one for venous blood, deep grey matter and a lesion; no scan is formed of it | 3D world |
| B19 | Segmented acquisition and the order of the lines | The fast spin echo of a console that lists it fills k-space in shots of one line per echo, in centric or linear order, and the image is formed with the amplitude of each line; every other sequence acquires its lines in one order, one per repetition (echo-planar: one shot) | core in the console |
| B20 | Three-dimensional encoding: a second phase-encode axis, the slab | A non-selective 3D scan is priced and its central partition is imaged; no slab profile, no fold along the slab | 3D world |
| C1 | Field strength: what changes between 1.5 T and 3 T | Two field strengths, one per session; nothing below 1.5 T or above 3 T | ordinary engine work |
| C4 | Shimming | The two in-plane linear terms can be set for a scan; there is no term through the slice, none above first order and no automatic shim. The 3D field library fits a shim of first or second order (nine solid harmonics) over a volume, with a declared limit on each channel, and returns the fixed first-order shim of the engine on the engine's own field; a second-order setting at the console waits for the slice engine on the 3D world | 3D world |
| C5 | Magnetic susceptibility: the field around air and tissue boundaries | The scanner adds the field of a few air spheres in closed form; it does not compute the field from the susceptibility of the object. The 3D field library does, with the dipole kernel, for any distribution of susceptibility (checked on a sphere, cylinders, a shell and a spheroid, and run on the seeded 3D head); no scan uses that field yet | 3D world |
| C8 | Adiabatic pulses: an inversion that tolerates the transmit field | The console's inversion is one efficiency number; the hyperbolic-secant pulse and its threshold are computed in the design layer and played by no sequence | core in the console |
| C9 | RF pulse design: shaping a pulse to a profile | A task asks for a slice-selective excitation and the scan rfscan plays a stored design through a modelled transmit chain (scale, amplifier compression, gradient delay, off-resonance); refocusing, inversion and variable-rate designs are generated and simulated only, nothing relaxes during a pulse, and the duration is compared with a reference search because no tight bound is proven | ordinary engine work |
| C17 | Gradient non-linearity: distortion away from the isocentre | Positions are scaled by one declared term, 1 - g (r / 250 mm)^2, the same along both axes, and the brightness does not change with it; there is no expansion of a real coil, nothing along z and no correction of the distortion | ordinary engine work |
| C20 | Spoiler and crusher gradients: the moment and what survives it | The spoiler moment of a gradient echo is a parameter and acts on the signal; the crushers of a spin echo are ideal: what they dephase is gone, so there is no stimulated echo. The echo trains and the diffusion-weighted spin echo of a console that lists them play real crushers inside a repetition, with the stimulated echoes they leave, and an ideal one at its end (what that leaves out is measured: up to 0.16 of an echo for a fluid). A spoiler played as a lobe with its own duration is computed by the signal core and served by no sequence | core in the console |
| C22 | RF power: what raises B1+rms, and its limit | The console prices RF as B1+rms against a limit, from the nominal flip angle times the transmit factor of the scan (`tx_scale`); it has no figure in W/kg. The field model computes the power a body absorbs for a given B1+ and how it grows with the square of the frequency; the console does not use it | field model |
| C33 | Agreement with measurement: a phantom on a real scanner against the same phantom here | Statistics of images, region signals and fitted values of public phantom sessions are compared with the engine's model of the same protocol (for an echo train with the design layer and with the multi-echo spin echo of the console), and the differences found are listed; no image of the console's sequences has been compared pixel by pixel with a scan of the same object | measured data |
| D16 | Ghosts of periodic motion along the phase-encode axis | One tissue class pulses or shifts periodically; no irregular motion, and nothing moves through the slice | 3D world |

"Computed" in the third column: the package already computes the item and checks it against a closed form or a second method, and no console sequence, parameter or task reaches it yet; [the checks](#the-check-behind-every-item-that-is-formed-formed-in-part-or-computed) name the rows.

### 3D world

A seeded volume with structure through the slice (a head, a test object) that gives a plane at any position and tilt, and the field of its susceptibility in 3D with a shim, exist as libraries; still to do: the slice engine that scans the volume (a slice selected in it, several slices, volume encoding).

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A24 | Perfusion: passage of a bolus, arterial spin labelling | - | No blood arrives through the plane and no tissue changes during the session; the vessels of the 3D head carry a direction and a speed as numbers only, and nothing flows until a slice engine uses them |
| A26 | Quantitative susceptibility mapping | computed | What exists, in the 3D field library: the forward model from a susceptibility distribution to its field, the phase of several echoes from that field, and one reference inversion, truncated division in k-space, which on a sphere without noise gives the known underestimate. What does not: removal of the background field, masks, unwrapping of the phase, any regularised inversion, and a scan that gives the phase of a volume (the scanner knows the field in one slice) |
| B4 | Several slices: slices per repetition, gap, order | - | A scan is one slice; the pulses of neighbouring slices are not played. A seeded 3D world that gives a plane at any position exists as a library; the slice engine that scans it is the missing part |
| B5 | Slice position, oblique planes, planning in three planes | - | The object of a scan is one axial section. The seeded 3D worlds (a head, a test object) give axial, sagittal, coronal and tilted planes as a library, but no scan is formed of them: the slice engine is the missing part |
| C30 | Phantom tests: slice thickness and slice position | - | The test objects of the scanner are flat. A 3D test object with ramps and crossed wedges through the slice exists as a library (drawn angles, not the dimensions of the ACR phantom); no scan is formed of it: the slice engine is the missing part |
| D19 | Cross-talk between neighbouring slices | - | A scan is one slice. The 3D world exists as a library; neighbouring slices excited in one repetition take the slice engine |
| D20 | Metal: distortion of the slice itself, and the sequences against it | - | The slice is flat: how it bends near metal takes the third dimension. The 3D field library computes the field of a susceptibility distribution to first order (enough for titanium, not for steel); no world holds metal and no slice is selected in such a field |

### Receive array

Several receive channels with sensitivity maps and noise correlation, the multi-channel data, coil combination and SENSE exist as a library; still to do: the console serving them (a coil to choose, an acceleration factor, what a scan returns), and the methods that work in k-space.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| B22 | Parallel imaging: fewer lines, unfolded with the coil sensitivities | computed | The array library leaves out phase-encode lines (factors 2 to 4) and unfolds the image with the sensitivity maps (SENSE), with the g-factor in closed form and measured with repeated noise, for maps that are given (with maps estimated from a prescan the error is reported without a tolerance); the methods that work in k-space (GRAPPA) and the acceleration of several slices at once are not built, and the console has one receive channel and no acceleration factor |
| C11 | Receive arrays: coil elements, their combination, the choice of coil | computed | The array library gives a world several receive elements, each with a sensitivity map (loops, in the quasi-static limit) and a noise covariance between them, forms the multi-channel data and combines the channels (root sum of squares, the optimal combination, an adaptive one) with the SNR of each; the field model computes receive maps and their noise matrix from Maxwell's equations, and the two are not joined. The console has one receive channel: there is no coil to choose and no coil image is returned |

### Spin systems

The density-matrix simulator for coupled spins, with its spectroscopy sequences, metabolite basis and quantification, exists as a library; still to do: a voxel that holds metabolites in the scanner world and a spectroscopy sequence in the console.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A28 | Spectroscopy: single voxel and spectroscopic imaging | computed | The spin-system package computes what the single-voxel sequences PRESS, STEAM and semi-LASER leave of a metabolite, coupled protons included, with slice-selective refocusing pulses and the displacement of the selected slice by the chemical shift, and it fits a spectrum with a basis of metabolite spectra; the scanner world has no voxel that holds metabolites, the console has no spectroscopy sequence and returns images of water and fat only, and spectroscopic imaging is not computed |
| A31 | J-coupling: multiplets, the echo of a coupled spin, spectral editing | computed | The spin-system package computes the multiplets of weakly and strongly coupled protons, how the echo of a coupled spin depends on the echo time, the edited difference of MEGA-PRESS for GABA and lactate and two-dimensional J-resolved signals; every tissue of the scanner is a set of uncoupled lines, and no console sequence acquires a spectrum or plays an editing pulse |
| A32 | Metabolite quantification: fitting a basis set, water referencing | computed | The spin-system package simulates a basis of metabolite spectra for a sequence, fits a spectrum as a sum of them with one shift, one width and one phase, gives the Cramer-Rao bounds of the fit and turns an amplitude into a concentration with the water signal as reference; it has fitted its own simulated spectra only: the scanner returns no spectrum, and neither macromolecules nor a baseline are in the basis or in the fit |

### Field model

Maxwell's equations on the slice for a body and a coil (B1+, B1-, SAR, RF shimming) exist as a library, in two dimensions; still to do: the scanner imaging and pricing RF with these fields instead of its declared patterns, and the third dimension.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| C34 | RF fields in the body: B1+ and B1- from Maxwell's equations, the wavelength in tissue, dielectric effects | computed | The field model solves Maxwell's equations on the slice for the tissues of a world and the currents of a coil: B1+ and B1-, the wavelength in tissue, the central brightening at 7 T and its near absence at 1.5 T. It has two dimensions, with fields that do not change along z (no end rings, no end of the head), and the scanner still images with declared transmit and receive patterns |
| C36 | Electrical properties from the transmit field: mapping conductivity and permittivity | computed | The field model recovers conductivity and permittivity from a complex B1+ map by the Helmholtz relation, inside a uniform region and without noise, and shows where that fails: at a boundary, and with the transceive-phase assumption for a coil of few rungs or a linear coil. The transmit pattern of the scanner is declared and does not come from the conductivity and permittivity of its tissues, so a scan holds nothing to recover; neither noise nor the third dimension is treated |
| C23 | SAR in the body: whole-body and local heating | computed | The field model computes the power a body absorbs on the slice from the electric field of the coil: SAR at a point, averaged over a square of 21.5 mm (its stand-in for the 10 g average: a definition of the package, not that of a standard) and averaged over the slice. It has two dimensions: no end rings, no neck or shoulders, no whole-body figure; no temperature is computed and no number of it is a safety figure. The console still prices RF as B1+rms only |
| C35 | RF shimming and parallel transmission: channel weights for a uniform B1+ inside limits on power and SAR | computed | The field model computes static RF shimming: the weights of the channels of a transmit array, phase only or magnitude and phase, that make B1+ uniform over a region under limits on power and on local SAR, and the trade-off between uniformity and the SAR limit. Pulses that differ between the channels (spatially selective parallel transmission) are not built, the fields are two-dimensional, and the scanner has one transmit channel with a declared pattern |
| C26 | Implants and devices: scanning inside the conditions of a label | - | No object holds a device and no task states a label. The field model stops short of the heating at a device: its electric field has one component, along z, on a grid of millimetres |

### Core in the console

The signal core over lists of blocks (Bloch ensemble, phase graphs, periodic solve) is behind the console: a sequence registry, image formation with an amplitude that changes from line to line, and four sequences (fast and multi-echo spin echo, multi-echo gradient echo, diffusion-weighted spin echo) on a console whose card lists them; still to do: the tool layer of the environments offering them to an agent, the other sequences of the core's library (prepared trains, two pools, real spoilers, what survives a repetition), and the six sequences of every console on the core.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A13 | Approach to the steady state: dummy cycles and the first lines of a scan | computed | The transient is computed by a separate chain of rotations and, in the signal core, by stepping a list of blocks from equilibrium or along a prepared train; the scanner serves every line at the steady state |
| A15 | Magnetisation preparation: saturation recovery, T2 preparation, prepared gradient echo | computed | An inversion-prepared gradient echo exists as a checked formula, and the signal core computes a prepared train of gradient echoes, T2 preparation and saturation recovery from lists of blocks; the console prepares with inversion before a spin echo and with fat saturation only |
| A19 | Spatial saturation bands | - | There is no spatial saturation pulse |
| A20 | Magnetisation transfer and chemical exchange | computed | The signal core computes two exchanging pools: magnetisation transfer with a saturation pulse on the bound pool, in a gradient echo and under continuous irradiation (the direct effect of the pulse on free water is left out), and chemical exchange between its evaluators only, against no closed form and in no sequence of its library; each tissue of the scanner is one pool of protons and no console sequence saturates a bound pool |
| A22 | Flow: inflow, time-of-flight angiography, velocity encoding | - | Nothing flows: blood is a static tissue |
| C21 | Gradient programs: lobes, moments and their nulling, the shortest waveform inside the limits | computed | The design layer computes moments, k-space and limit checks of a gradient program and the shortest lobe for given moments; the console builds its own trapezoids and no waveform can be entered |
| C24 | Nerve stimulation: the limit on dB/dt | computed | The design layer computes a stimulation figure of a gradient program from a declared model; the console plays gradients at one fixed slew rate and has no such limit |

### Realistic anatomy

Textured digital anatomy instead of classes of one value each.

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| B26 | Reconstruction from incomplete data: compressed sensing and learned methods | - | The reconstruction is fixed, and objects made of classes of one value have no texture to judge such a method on |

### Ordinary engine work

| | Item | In the package | What is missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| A23 | Contrast agents: relaxivity and concentration | - | No material carries an agent; a dilution series could be built from vials |
| A27 | BOLD contrast and functional MRI | - | No tissue changes its T2* during the session, and a scan is not repeated as a series |
| B21 | Radial and spiral trajectories | - | Sampling is Cartesian |
| B24 | Options of the reconstruction: zero filling, filters, intensity and distortion correction | - | The reconstruction is fixed, with nothing to choose: the unfiltered transform of the acquired matrix, and homodyne detection where part of k-space was left out |
| B25 | Raw data: looking at k-space, spikes | - | Only images leave the scanner |
| C13 | Receiver gain and dynamic range | - | Samples are floating-point numbers: no converter, no clipping |
| C19 | Eddy currents and concomitant fields | - | Gradients are played as ideal trapezoids |
| C25 | Acoustic noise of the gradients | - | There is no model of sound |
| C27 | The static field around the magnet: fringe field, forces on objects, zones, screening | - | The field outside the bore and the force on an object in it are not modelled: this is the field of the magnet itself, which neither the RF field model nor the susceptibility field in 3D holds |
| C32 | Stability over time: field drift, repeated scans | - | The system does not change during a session; a repeated scan differs by its noise only |
| D18 | Gating, triggering and breath-holding against motion | - | The console has no trigger: a scan is not synchronised with the motion |

## Where the list comes from

The items were drawn up from the tables of contents of 7 textbooks and from 10 teaching and examination outlines, read at the level of their headings. They are a map of topics; no examination item is reproduced.

- Bernstein, King, Zhou, Handbook of MRI Pulse Sequences
- Brown, Cheng, Haacke, Thompson, Venkatesan, Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Physical Principles and Sequence Design, 2nd ed.
- Nishimura, Principles of Magnetic Resonance Imaging
- McRobbie, Moore, Graves, Prince, MRI from Picture to Proton, 3rd ed.
- Liang, Lauterbur, Principles of Magnetic Resonance Imaging: A Signal Processing Perspective
- Dale, Brown, Semelka, MRI: Basic Principles and Applications, 5th ed.
- Westbrook, Talbot, MRI in Practice, 5th ed.
- ARRT, MRI examination content specifications (2025)
- ABR, qualifying (core) exam physics study guide, section 13 (2023)
- AAPM, diagnostic radiology residents physics curriculum, module 13 (2018)
- AAPM Report 197, graduate programmes, section 3.2.5
- EFOMP, core curriculum for medical physicists in radiology, section 13 (2011)
- ASRT / AEIRS / SMRT, magnetic resonance curriculum (2015)
- IAEA, Diagnostic Radiology Physics handbook, chapters 14 and 15, with TCS-47
- ISMRM, weekend courses MR Physics and Engineering, Artifacts, Image Reconstruction (2022)
- ESMRMB, Practical MR Physics (2025)
- AAPM Report 100 with the ACR quality-control tests
